questions.q: In a laboratory in Owerri, a ray of light travelling in kerosene of refractive index 1.44 strikes the kerosene–air boundary at an angle of 25.0° to the normal. Calculate the angle of refraction in air, correct to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: Using Snell’s law, 1.44 sin25.0° = 1.00 sin r, so sin r = 0.6086 and r = 37.5°. Dividing sin25.0° by 1.44 would give 17.1°, which is the common mistake of using the refractive index the wrong way round.

questions.q: Two forces of 6.0 N and 8.0 N act at a point with an angle of 60° between them. Calculate the magnitude of their resultant, correct to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: For two forces at an angle θ, R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ. Here R² = 6.0² + 8.0² + 2(6.0)(8.0)cos60° = 36 + 64 + 48 = 148, so R = √148 = 12.2 N. The value 10.0 N would be obtained if the forces were perpendicular.

questions.q: A hunter in Oyo claps his hands and hears the echo from a cliff 1.6 s later. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how far is the hunter from the cliff?
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so the total distance is speed × time = 340 × 1.6 = 544 m. The one-way distance is half of this, 544 ÷ 2 = 272 m; using 544 m forgets the return journey.

questions.q: A tricycle in Aba starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 15 m/s in 5.0 s. It then travels at a constant speed of 15 m/s for 12 s. Calculate the total distance travelled.
questions.explanation: During acceleration, s = ((0 + 15)/2) × 5.0 = 37.5 m. At constant speed, s = 15 × 12 = 180 m, giving a total of 37.5 + 180 = 217.5 m. Ignoring the acceleration stage gives 180 m.

questions.q: A converging lens of focal length 15.0 cm is used as a magnifying glass to view a small print placed 10.0 cm from the lens. Calculate the magnitude of the magnification produced.
questions.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives 1/v = 1/15 − 1/10 = −1/30, so v = −30 cm. The magnification magnitude is |v|/u = 30/10 = 3.0. The value 0.60 arises if 1/15 and 1/10 are added instead of subtracted.

questions.q: An open pipe in a music class in Ilorin has an effective length of 0.40 m. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, what is the fundamental frequency of the pipe?
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, the fundamental wavelength is λ = 2L = 2 × 0.40 = 0.80 m. Therefore f = v/λ = 340/0.80 = 425 Hz; a closed pipe of the same length would have half this frequency.

questions.q: A minibus in Kaduna covers 10 m during the 2nd second of its motion and 20 m during the 4th second while accelerating uniformly. Calculate its acceleration.
questions.explanation: The distance covered in the nth second is sₙ = u + (a/2)(2n − 1). For the 2nd second, u + 3a/2 = 10; for the 4th second, u + 7a/2 = 20. Subtracting gives 2a = 10, so a = 5.0 m/s².

questions.q: In a physics demonstration in Ibadan, a plane mirror is turned through 10° while the incident ray remains fixed. Through what angle does the reflected ray turn?
questions.explanation: When a plane mirror turns through an angle θ, its normal also turns through θ. For a fixed incident ray, the reflected ray turns through 2θ, so here the angle is 2 × 10° = 20°.

questions.q: A stone is projected horizontally with a speed of 15 m/s from the top of a tower 45 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s², how far from the foot of the tower does the stone land?
questions.explanation: The time of fall depends on the vertical motion: h = ½gt², so 45 = ½ × 10 × t², giving t = √9 = 3 s. The horizontal distance is speed × time = 15 × 3 = 45 m.

questions.q: A pulley system in a rice mill in Uyo has velocity ratio 5.0. An effort of 240 N raises a load of 900 N. What is the efficiency of the system?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 900 N ÷ 240 N = 3.75. Efficiency = (mechanical advantage ÷ velocity ratio) × 100% = (3.75 ÷ 5.0) × 100% = 75%. Using effort ÷ load instead gives about 26.7%, which is not the efficiency.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas in a sealed syringe in Ibadan occupies 250 cm³ at a pressure of 1.20 × 10⁵ Pa. If the pressure is reduced to 0.80 × 10⁵ Pa at constant temperature, what volume does the gas occupy?
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so V₂ = (1.20 × 10⁵ × 250) ÷ (0.80 × 10⁵) = 375 cm³. The pressure falls, so the volume must rise; 167 cm³ results from using the pressure ratio upside down.

questions.q: A balloon contains 500 cm³ of air at 27°C in Jos. It is cooled to -3°C at constant pressure. What is its new volume?
questions.explanation: Convert the temperatures to kelvin: T₁ = 27 + 273 = 300 K and T₂ = -3 + 273 = 270 K. At constant pressure, V₂ = V₁T₂ ÷ T₁ = 500 × 270 ÷ 300 = 450 cm³. Inverting the temperature ratio gives about 556 cm³, not the new volume.

questions.q: A gas at 27 °C and 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa is heated to 127 °C while its volume is doubled. Calculate its final pressure.
questions.explanation: Using P₁V₁ ÷ T₁ = P₂V₂ ÷ T₂, with T₁ = 300 K, T₂ = 400 K and V₂ = 2V₁, gives P₂ = 1.0 × 10⁵ × 400 ÷ (300 × 2) = 6.67 × 10⁴ Pa. If the doubling of volume is ignored, the result would be 1.33 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: An electron moving at 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s enters a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.30 T perpendicular to the field. Calculate the magnetic force on the electron. (Take e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.)
questions.explanation: For motion perpendicular to the field, magnetic force F = qvB = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)(2.0 × 10⁶)(0.30) = 9.6 × 10⁻¹⁴ N. Multiplying only the charge by the flux density gives 4.8 × 10⁻²⁰ N, which omits the speed.

questions.q: A coil of 80 turns has the magnetic flux through each turn changing uniformly from 2.0 × 10⁻³ Wb to 8.0 × 10⁻³ Wb in 0.20 s. Calculate the induced emf.
questions.explanation: The change in flux per turn is (8.0 − 2.0) × 10⁻³ = 6.0 × 10⁻³ Wb. For 80 turns, the rate of change of flux linkage is 80 × 6.0 × 10⁻³ ÷ 0.20 = 2.4 V. Omitting the number of turns gives 0.030 V.

questions.q: A micrometer screw gauge in a workshop in Sokoto has a zero error of −0.02 mm. When it is used to measure the diameter of a wire, the reading is 5.48 mm. What is the correct diameter of the wire?
questions.explanation: A negative zero error means the gauge reads 0.02 mm less than the true value, so the correction is added. Correct diameter = 5.48 + 0.02 = 5.50 mm. Subtracting instead gives 5.46 mm and treats the negative zero error with the wrong sign.

questions.q: A technician in Aba measures the diameter of a fine wire as 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ m. Express this diameter in micrometres (μm).
questions.explanation: Since 1 μm = 1 × 10⁻⁶ m, divide the length in metres by 1 × 10⁻⁶: (2.5 × 10⁻⁵) ÷ (1 × 10⁻⁶) = 25. Therefore the diameter is 25 μm. A common power-of-ten slip gives 2.5 μm instead.

questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.30 Ω is connected to a 2.7 Ω resistor. What is the terminal potential difference of the cell?
questions.explanation: The current is I = 1.5 ÷ (2.7 + 0.30) = 0.50 A. The terminal potential difference is V = IR = 0.50 × 2.7 = 1.35 V, which is also e.m.f. minus lost volts. A value of 1.50 V would be obtained only if the internal resistance were ignored.

questions.q: When ²⁷₁₃Al is bombarded with an alpha particle and emits a neutron, the product nucleus formed is
questions.explanation: For the reaction, mass number balance gives 27 + 4 = A + 1, so A = 30. Atomic number balance gives 13 + 2 = Z + 0, so Z = 15; the element with atomic number 15 is phosphorus, ³⁰₁₅P.

questions.q: In a ripple tank experiment in Enugu, a transverse water wave is represented by y = 0.04 sin(60πt − 3πx), where y is in metres, t in seconds and x in metres. What is the speed of the wave?
questions.explanation: Comparing with y = A sin(ωt − kx), ω = 60π rad/s and k = 3π rad/m. The wave speed is v = ω/k = 60π ÷ 3π = 20 m/s.

questions.q: A guitar string in Tunde's room is sounded together with a tuning fork of frequency 384 Hz. Five beats per second are heard. When the tension of the string is slightly increased, the beat frequency decreases to 2 Hz. What is the original frequency of the string?
questions.explanation: The original string frequency differs from 384 Hz by 5 Hz, so it is either 379 Hz or 389 Hz. Increasing the tension raises the string frequency; only starting from 379 Hz can the beat frequency fall from 5 Hz to 2 Hz, namely when the string rises to 382 Hz.

questions.q: A copper wire of original length 1.50 m and cross-sectional area 4.0 × 10⁻⁷ m² is stretched by a tensile force of 20 N. If the Young modulus of copper is 1.2 × 10¹¹ Pa, what is the extension produced?
questions.explanation: Stress = F/A = 20 ÷ (4.0 × 10⁻⁷) = 5.0 × 10⁷ Pa. Strain = stress ÷ Young modulus = (5.0 × 10⁷) ÷ (1.2 × 10¹¹) = 4.17 × 10⁻⁴, so extension = strain × original length = 4.17 × 10⁻⁴ × 1.50 = 6.25 × 10⁻⁴ m.

questions.q: A mercury barometer in Calabar reads 750 mmHg. Taking the density of mercury as 1.36 × 10⁴ kg/m³ and g = 10 m/s², what atmospheric pressure does this correspond to?
questions.explanation: The height is 750 mm = 0.750 m. Atmospheric pressure is p = ρgh = 1.36 × 10⁴ × 10 × 0.750 = 1.02 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: A 12 μF capacitor is charged to 50 V and then disconnected from the battery. It is connected across an uncharged 6.0 μF capacitor. What is the common potential difference across the capacitors?
questions.explanation: The charge before connection is Q = CV = 12 μF × 50 V = 600 μC. After connection the total capacitance is 12 μF + 6.0 μF = 18 μF, so the common voltage is V = Q/C = 600 μC ÷ 18 μF = 33.3 V.

questions.q: A step-index optical fibre has a core of refractive index 1.60 and a cladding of refractive index 1.40. Calculate, to the nearest degree, the critical angle at the core–cladding boundary.
questions.explanation: For total internal reflection at the core–cladding boundary, sin c = n_cladding/n_core = 1.40/1.60 = 0.875. Thus c = sin⁻¹(0.875) ≈ 61°, to the nearest degree. Using the ratio upside down would give a value greater than 1, which is impossible for a sine.

questions.q: A stamp is placed 6.0 cm from a converging lens of focal length 8.0 cm. Determine the nature and position of the image.
options: 24 cm from the lens on the same side as the stamp, virtual and erect
3.4 cm from the lens on the opposite side, real and inverted
24 cm from the lens on the opposite side, real and inverted
48 cm from the lens on the same side as the stamp, virtual and erect
questions.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = 1/8.0 − 1/6.0 = −1/24, so v = −24 cm. The negative sign means the image is virtual and on the same side of the lens as the stamp, at 24 cm from the lens.

questions.q: A ray of white light enters a glass prism. Which colour travels fastest through the glass?
questions.explanation: In glass, the refractive index is least for red light because red has the longest wavelength. Since speed in the medium is v = c/n, the colour with the smallest refractive index travels fastest, so red travels fastest. Violet is deviated most but is slowed most.

questions.q: Two forces of magnitude 40 N and 30 N act at a point with an angle of 120° between them. Calculate the magnitude of their resultant.
questions.explanation: For two forces at an angle θ, R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ. Here R² = 40² + 30² + 2(40)(30) cos 120° = 1600 + 900 − 1200 = 1300, so R = √1300 ≈ 36.1 N. Treating the forces as perpendicular would wrongly give 50.0 N.

questions.q: Which of the following groups contains only vector quantities?
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction. Displacement, impulse and electric field intensity all have direction, so that group contains only vectors. Speed is a scalar, mass is a scalar, and work, energy and power are all scalars.

questions.q: A car sounding a horn of frequency 480 Hz moves directly away from a stationary observer at 24 m/s. If the speed of sound in air is 336 m/s, calculate the frequency heard by the observer.
questions.explanation: For a source moving away from a stationary observer, f′ = f v/(v + v_s). Thus f′ = 480 × 336/(336 + 24) = 480 × 336/360 = 448 Hz. The observer hears a lower frequency, as expected when the source recedes.

questions.q: A sound wave of frequency 425 Hz travels in air with speed 340 m/s. It then enters water, where its speed is 1360 m/s. What is its wavelength in water?
questions.explanation: When sound passes from one medium to another, its frequency remains unchanged. λ = v/f = 1360/425 = 3.20 m in water. The wavelength in air would be 340/425 = 0.80 m, but the question asks for water.

questions.q: A ball is rolled horizontally from the top of a table 1.25 m high with speed 4.0 m/s. How far from the foot of the table does it land? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: The vertical fall time is found from h = ½gt², so t = √(2h/g) = √(2 × 1.25/10) = √0.25 = 0.50 s. The horizontal distance is x = ut = 4.0 × 0.50 = 2.0 m, because horizontal velocity stays constant.

questions.q: A tricycle in Kano travelling at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly to rest in 10 s. Calculate the distance it travels during the first 4 s of braking.
questions.explanation: The deceleration is a = (0 − 20)/10 = −2.0 m/s². For the first 4 s, s = ut + ½at² = 20(4) + ½(−2)(4²) = 80 − 16 = 64 m. Equivalently, the speed after 4 s is 12 m/s, and average speed is (20 + 12)/2 = 16 m/s over 4 s.

questions.q: An ideal gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27°C and a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. What volume will it occupy at 327°C and a pressure of 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa?
questions.explanation: Using V₂ = P₁V₁T₂ ÷ (P₂T₁), convert the temperatures to kelvin: 300 K and 600 K. Thus V₂ = (1.0 × 10⁵ × 300 × 600) ÷ (1.5 × 10⁵ × 300) = 400 cm³. Ignoring the pressure change would give 600 cm³.

questions.q: A sealed gas cylinder contains gas at a pressure of 2.4 × 10⁵ Pa at 27°C. It is taken into a cold store where the temperature is -23°C. Assuming the volume remains constant, what is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: For a fixed mass at constant volume, P₂ = P₁T₂ ÷ T₁. The temperatures are 300 K and 250 K, so P₂ = 2.4 × 10⁵ × 250 ÷ 300 = 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Inverting the temperature ratio would wrongly give 2.88 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: The density of a metal sample is 8.0 g/cm³. What is this density in kg/m³?
questions.explanation: Since 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³, because 1 g = 10⁻³ kg and 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³, then 8.0 g/cm³ = 8.0 × 1000 = 8000 kg/m³.

questions.q: A micrometer screw gauge has a zero error of +0.003 cm. The reading obtained when measuring the thickness of a metal sheet is 0.248 cm. What is the corrected thickness?
questions.explanation: A positive zero error means the gauge reads greater than the true value by 0.003 cm. The corrected thickness is therefore 0.248 − 0.003 = 0.245 cm. Adding the zero error would overcorrect the reading.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns and area 0.030 m² is placed with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The flux density is reduced uniformly from 0.80 T to 0.20 T in 0.12 s. Calculate the average induced emf in the coil.
questions.explanation: The change in flux density is 0.80 − 0.20 = 0.60 T, so the flux change per turn is 0.030 × 0.60 = 0.018 Wb. For 200 turns the total flux change is 200 × 0.018 = 3.6 Wb, and dividing by 0.12 s gives 30 V. Using only one turn would give 0.15 V.

questions.q: A straight wire of length 0.25 m carrying a current of 2.0 A is placed at 30° to a uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.40 T. Calculate the magnetic force on the wire.
questions.explanation: The force is F = BIL sin θ = 0.40 × 2.0 × 0.25 × sin 30° = 0.10 N. Omitting the sine factor gives 0.20 N, which is too large.

questions.q: A screw jack used in an auto workshop in Uyo has a pitch of 0.50 cm. Its handle is 35 cm long, measured from the axis. Taking π = 22/7, what is its velocity ratio?
questions.explanation: The velocity ratio of a screw jack is VR = 2πL ÷ p, where L is the handle length and p is the pitch. Thus VR = 2 × (22/7) × 35 ÷ 0.50 = 440. Omitting the factor 2 gives 220.
